title: Streaking Bacteria on an Agar Plate from a Glycerol Stock
author: Cristian Riccio
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.5xig7ke
materials: Rub the loop in the glycerol stock.
Sterilise the loop in the flame.

steps.title: Prepare Glycerol Stock
steps.instruction: Transfer the glycerol stock onto dry ice next to a flame.

steps.title: Streak Bacteria on Agar Plate
steps.instruction: Perform a streak plate procedure to isolate colonies using a zigzag pattern.

substeps.instruction: Streak the bacteria in a zigzag pattern over the first half of the agar plate.
Zigzag over the next section of the plate, overlapping with the first half by a quarter of a plate.
Zigzag over the final section of the plate, overlapping with the second half by a quarter of a plate.

steps.title: Incubate Plate
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate overnight at the optimal temperature for bacterial growth (e.g., 37°C for E. coli).

steps.title: Verify Colony Growth
steps.instruction: Check the plate the next day for the presence of single colonies visible on a quarter or half of the plate.
